newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse to launch derivatives in '97 - Pres.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse to launch derivatives in '97 - Pres.

text.p: The Athens stock exchange will launch trading in derivatives this year, starting with a stock-index contract on a basket of 20-25 liquid blue-chip shares, bourse president Manolis Xanthakis said on Wednesday.
The launch of trading in derivatives would improve the market's liquidity and expand its investment horizon, Xanthakis told a conference organised by the Economist magazine.
"The first product to be launched in Greece's capital market will be a futures contract on an index of 20-25 highly liquid shares," he said.
Similar statements had been made by bourse authorities during a roadshow in Boston last year.
Xanthakis also pointed out that share dematerialisation, which will allow electronic paperless settlement, is expected to be completed by year-end 1997.
"Replacing physical delivery of shares with electronic book entry will improve transparency and reduce the time it now takes to settle transactions," he said.

Trading volume in the first quarter of 1997 at the Athens bourse was up 95 percent compared to the first quarter a year earlier, amounting to 969 billion drachmas -- 48 percent of the exchange's total trading volume last year, he said.
Turnover will be further boosted by the launch of electronic screen trading in bonds which the exchange plans to introduce by June this year.
"Member brokers' staff are currently being trained on the new system. The official launch is planned for early June," Xanthakis said.

The counter-inflationary policy in recent years saw a dramatic fall in inflation and interest rates, bringing the average real T-bill rate in 1996 below 4.0 percent when the market's dividend yield was 4.5 percent, he said.
"The reason behind the stock market's rise was the improvement in macroeconomic indicators and the revision of stock market regulations," he said.

The stock exchange centre in Thessaloniki, which already trades all listings on the Athens bourse, plans to list fast-growing northern Greek companies and attract investment capital from the wider Balkan area.

Xanthakis said the legal framework for the introduction of Greek depositary receipts had already been set up. "These will be the investment mechanism for listing Balkan companies on the Athens bourse," he told the conference.
